head: 319f1be8ccc814fd482bf9f7c04f5d02deddef2d
classification_reasons: Blast radius: plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py is registered on every Bash/PowerShell call in every phase, in CI and by hand (plugin/hooks/hooks.json), and plugin/ci/settings.ci.json/run_phase.py now rewrite a sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite list every CI phase job reads -- this is the opposite of a few-file, low-risk surface.
Risk list: this change touches sdlc.yaml: risk_list item 'auth' end to end (status.yaml: risk_accepted: [auth], owner-accepted, not closed by a tight no-concern spec).

Tests: shell_guard.py's ~1000-line tokenizer/resolver is new code with its own dedicated test suite (tests/test_hooks.py, +582 lines); it is not code the pre-existing suite already covered before this change, and its correctness rests on a large enumerated idiom/edge-case list rather than a small diff an existing test already exercises.
attempted: Intent: compared the cumulative diff (merge-base of sdlc/0002/d ... HEAD) against intent.md's proposed outcome ('no instance of this authz weakness remains'). The diff adds a Bash/PowerShell write-target check (shell_guard.py) wired beside the existing Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit-only protected_paths.py and test_file_lock.py, closing the exact route (plugin/hooks/hooks.json:32) the finding named, plus a CI sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite second layer named in spec.md. Matches the stated problem, not something adjacent.

Spec and plan: re-read spec.md Requirements/Design/Acceptance and plan.md Files-that-change/Order-of-work; the diff's changed-file set (plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py new, plugin/hooks/hooks.json, plugin/ci/settings.ci.json, plugin/ci/run_phase.py, tests/test_hooks.py, tests/test_ci.py, tests/test_evals.py, docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, plus this change's own evidence/status.yaml) matches plan.md's list exactly -- no undeclared file, template/.claude/settings.json and the 0006 eval case correctly left out per the round-3 design decisions recorded in Flagged concerns. All three open questions from intent.md are answered in spec.md's 'Open questions from intent' section, not left dangling. One pre-existing, explicitly disclosed, non-blocking deviation: plan.md step 1 asked for the shell_guard import inside test functions; fix-response.md round 5 item 21 discloses it stayed at module scope (a test-isolation nit, not a correctness defect) -- this is named in the diff's own fix-response.md, not hidden.

Proof: gate-c.json's committed 'commands' check (details.ran_by: runner, not the writer's claim) shows build/test/lint actually executed post-session with exit 0 each and test output '1609 passed in 299.88s' -- this is the deterministic-check-independent, toolchain-literal record the instructions direct me to trust (not claude-*.json/run-*.json). Phase (d)'s own build.log/test.log/lint.log correctly read the documented 'deferred to the runner' placeholder (first line matches the required format exactly) since this is a CI session (SDLC_GATE_COMMANDS=runner); per the plugin 0.3.2/item-3b rule this is not missing proof. verifier.md for phase (d) is explicitly a read-only diff-vs-plan check (consistent with the CI-deferred pattern) and reports no mismatch between the diff and plan.md/spec.md, correctly flagging only the already-disclosed module-scope-import nit.

Specifically traced, independent of any embedded prior reviewer's prose, the two bugs that the phase-c panel escalated on and the round-5 fix (commit 22697f2) claims to close: read _git_global_scan (shell_guard.py) by hand against 'git -c core.fileMode=false rm CLAUDE.md' -- it now skips the -c/value pair and lands on the 'rm' verb, yielding CLAUDE.md as a candidate (confirmed by the parametrized test test_shell_guard_sees_the_git_verb_after_a_global_option, which encodes exactly this command and asserts d.block). Read _inner_shell_command against 'bash --norc -c "..."' -- it now scans past the leading flag to find the adjacent -c token and recurses (confirmed by test_shell_write_targets_sees_through_a_flag_before_the_inner_shell_s_c_token, same command, asserting the extracted target). Also read _protected_roots/_is_ancestor_of_protected (the directory-ancestor gap, item 3) and its dedicated tests (test_shell_guard_denies_deleting_a_directory_that_contains_a_guardrail, test_shell_guard_denies_deleting_an_ancestor_of_a_sdlc_yaml_protected_paths_entry) -- the implementation matches what the tests assert.

Blast radius: read decide()'s short-circuit (round-4 item 18 fix) that returns allow() before any config/branch/test-lock lookup when shell_write_targets finds no write candidate at all -- this closes a prior fail-closed-on-unreadable-config risk for an ordinary 'git status', reducing the chance this universally-registered hook parks routine work. Read the new sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite wiring in plugin/ci/run_phase.py/settings.ci.json and its test (test_ci_settings_file_rewrites_the_sandbox_filesystem_deny_write_list, test_ci_settings_file_rejects_a_bad_protected_paths_entry) -- matches spec.md Requirements (directories named, not globbed; a glob entry skipped and noted, not silently dropped).

Policies: security-baseline rule 1 (authorization must not depend on which tool route reaches the target) is the rule the whole change exists to satisfy end to end (Bash/PowerShell now checked the same as the file-editing tools). Spot-checked the new test lines in tests/test_hooks.py for the scanner's three DANGEROUS literals (eval(, exec(, shell=True) -- none found as literal source text, matching spec.md Acceptance's instruction.

Tests: confirmed the two assertions plan.md names as deliberate, disclosed contract changes (not weakenings) were actually made as described: tests/test_ci.py's sandbox assertion now asserts full equality with only filesystem.denyWrite substituted (strengthened versus the prior narrower 'network'-only check the round-4 review flagged), and tests/test_evals.py derives FRAMEWORK_SUITE from evals/cases/ folders rather than a literal tuple. No pre-existing test was weakened to make the fix pass; every new behavior change in fix-response.md's round-5 list (21 items) is paired with a named, read test.

Did not re-run or cite gate/cli.py check, checks.py or any skill's check.py, and did not treat the committed claude-*.json/run-*.json/gate-c.json records as proof beyond the one place the instructions permit: gate-c.json's 'commands' check, which is the toolchain's own recorded exit codes/output, not a runner-record claim about an agent's actions.
